summary: This state is sealed: its secret values are locked, and only the 4 members listed below can open them. Names, types and dependencies stay visible, so the graph and the plans keep working.

file.text: The access list (readers.txt) matches the state.

you.name: ada
you.text: You are ada and can open this state.

roles.text: The roles are locked in. Only an admin can change them, and every change is signed, so editing your own copy of the access list gives nobody extra rights. The access list asks for other roles than the ones saved.

issues.title: The access list asks for different roles
issues.text: The access list asks for other roles than the ones saved. An admin saves them to make them count.

suggestions.title: Save the new roles
suggestions.why: The access list asks for other roles than the state holds. An admin saves them as the next version, signed by an admin of the one before. When a key leaves or is demoted, the admin also vouches for the changes it already made, so those stay valid.

steps.text: It lists what changes and asks first.

suggestions.title: Add a member
suggestions.why: The new member makes a key and sends the line it prints (a CI job is a member too, with a key of its own). A current member adds the line, commits it and rewraps.
suggestions.who: the new member, then any member

steps.text: On the machine of the new member:
On the machine of a current member:

suggestions.title: Remove access for ada
suggestions.why: This removes you: once it has run you cannot open the state, and another member has to finish it. Use this when ada no longer needs the state. It stops new records being locked to their key. They keep what they have already read, and an old copy of the bucket still opens with their key, so replace any real secrets they could read where those secrets live.

steps.text: You can no longer open the state once this has run. A member who is left runs the rest, which seals every existing record again under the new key:

suggestions.title: Change the role of ada
suggestions.why: A role says what a member may do: an admin manages who has access and the roles, a writer can change the state, a reader can look and plan.

steps.text: In .pravo/access/readers.txt, change the last word of the line that starts with ada to role:admin, role:writer or role:reader.
git commit -m 'Change the role of ada'
It lists what changes and asks first.

suggestions.title: Set a recovery key
suggestions.why: A recovery key is split into shares, any K of which rebuild it, so that the state can still be opened when every member has lost their key. Give each share to a different person, offline. Whoever holds K shares can open the state, so K is a decision about whom to trust together.

steps.text: Make the key and the shares. This writes recovery-shares/ and .pravo/access/recovery.txt:
Do not commit recovery-shares/. Give each file to a different person, offline.

suggestions.title: Check the state
suggestions.why: The check hashes every record against its name and prints who can read the state.
